Timber Fire grows, Plaskett Fire takes hold in Big Sur
sources.text:
Timber Fire grows, Plaskett Fire takes hold in Big Sur
Gloomy skies stretched across Monterey County Thursday as two major wildfires burned along the Big Sur coast.
The Timber Fire swelled to nearly 20,000 acres and the fast-growing Plaskett Fire, ignited roughly 30 miles to the south, spurred evacuation orders.
Wildfire smoke from both incidents has pushed local air quality to hazardous levels along the coast and into adjacent valleys, according to public health officials who advise all impacted residents to keep windows and doors closed, utilize indoor air filtration systems and avoid strenuous outdoor activities.
To find the latest air quality information where you are, go to Monterey Bay Area Resource District. Or put in your location at AirNow.gov.
A section of Highway 1 has been closed by the California Highway Patrol (CHP) ahead of critical tactical operations.
As of 1 p.m. Thursday, Aug. 27, the highway will be closed to thru traffic between Andrew Molera State Park entrance and the Captain Cooper School entrance. Public safety officials advise motorists to stay off impacted roadways and do not attempt to travel through or return to closed areas.
For the latest highway closure information go to County of Monterey Alerts.
Public safety officials are advising anyone who needs evacuation assistance to call the virtual Temporary Evacuation Point at 831-647-7760.
A shelter will open at 5 p.m. on Aug. 27 at the Carmel Mission Inn Conference Room (3665 Rio Road, Carmel).
The Timber Fire in Big Sur has scorched 19,296 acres, as of 4:04 p.m. on Aug. 27, with containment dropping to 21%, according to a Cal Fire status report. More than 660 structures are threatened. According to fire officials, the "fire behavior remains moderate with no westward perimeter growth anticipated past Coast Ridge Road."
The Timbe Fire began "in a remote location with difficult access" at about 9:38 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 8, burning about 100 acres, the Los Padres National Forest said in a Facebook post.
The Plaskett Fire, which ignited Wednesday morning off Forest Road 23S10 east of Los Burros Road, has grown to 140 acres as of 4:29 p.m. on Aug. 27, according to a Cal Fire Status report, and is actively threatening structures. The fire is 0% contained.
According to fire officials, "due to local resource staging, air and ground assets were surged to the scene within minutes."
The causes of both fires are under investigation.
Timber Fire and Plaskett Fire evacuations
Evacuation orders are in place for the following zones: MRY-D082, MRY-D089, MRY-D090, MRY-D091, MRY-F015-B, MRY-F015-C, MRY-F022, MRY-F023-A, MRY-F025, MRY-F023-B, MRY-F028-B, MRY-F028-C, MRY-F029, MRY-F031-A, MRY-F035, MRY-F036
Evacuation warnings have been issued for the areas of: MRY-D078, MRY-D084, MRY-D085, MRY-D086, MRY-D088, MRY-F015-B, MRY-F018, MRY-F019, MRY-F020, MRY-F021-B, MRY-F024, MRY-F026, MRY-F027-A, MRY-F027-B, MRY-F028-A, MRY-F028-D, MRY-F030-A, MRY-F030-B, MRY-F031-B, MRY-F032-A, MRY-F032-B, MRY-F033, MRY-F034, MRY-F035, MRY-F037
Shelter in Place: MRY-F021-A, MRY-F021-B, MRY-F024, MRY-F026, MRY-F027-A
People under a Shelter in Place order and stay must be able to sustain themselves for at least 7 days, according to public safety officials. Otherwise, leave the area.
Information can change quickly. For the latest information on Evacuation Orders, Warnings and Shelter in Place advisories, go to County of Monterey Alerts.

sources.news_title: New Big Sur Wildfire, the Plaskett Fire, Breaks Out South of Timber Fire
sources.text:
A new, 40-acre wildfire began Wednesday morning near the Big Sur coast, about 27 miles south of the southernmost section of the still burning Timber Fire.
It's called the Plaskett Fire, and it began around 11 am Wednesday east of Los Burros Road, near the community of Plaskett, as KPIX reports. The fire had grown to 100 acres as of 2:15 pm, and was 0% contained.
An evacuation warning was issued for Plaskett and the area of the Plaskett Creek Campsite, and an evacuation order was issued for a zone to south and east, including a section of coast near Willow Creek Beach and San Martin Rock. The evacuation order is affecting around 30 residents, according to Cal Fire.
This new fire is burning in a different section of Los Padres National Forest that is more than 25 miles south of where the Timber Fire has been burning since August 8.
"Firefighters from various agencies including U.S. Forest Service, CAL FIRE, and local government are aggressively moving ground crews and heavy equipment to the perimeter of the Plaskett Fire in Monterey County to establish containment lines," Cal Fire said in a statement. "Specialized elite Hotshot crews are actively working to gain access to the fire's edge, while eight air tankers have been requested to fly overhead and assist ground personnel with targeted retardant drops."
Air resources are reportedly dropping water on the fire, which is burning "in very difficult terrain that is hard to access," and the fire has been growing at a "moderate" rate of speed, per Cal Fire.
On Wednesday afternoon, Cal Fire reported that eight structures were under threat from the fire. "After initially burning north-northwest, the fire crossed a drainage and is now working up the south side of a mountain following a slope reversal," the agency said.
Meanwhile, the Timber Fire stands at 23% containment, which is actually down from 25% on Monday. The fire has grown by 5,000 acres in two days, to 17,817 acres, burning uphill through the Lion Creek drainage to the north, and to the east near the North and South Forks of the Big Sur River. Hot and dry conditions have contributed to the fire's growth and will continue to, Cal Fire says.
Highway 1 remains open, however traffic controls were in place Wednesday as crews worked to clear rock debris left behind from Timber Fire operations which had piled up by the roadside. This meant periodic traffic holds of 10 to 15 minutes for those driving through the area.

sources.news_title: Plaskett Fire breaks out in California's Big Sur as crews continue battling Timber Fire
sources.text:
Plaskett Fire grows in California's Big Sur just south of Timber Fire; evacuations ordered
A new fire that broke out in California's Big Sur on Wednesday morning grew on Thursday, prompted evacuations just south of where crews have battled a massive wildfire that has burned for more than two weeks.
According to Cal Fire, the Plaskett Fire was first reported shortly after 11 a.m. off Forest Rd 23S10, east of Los Burros Road near the community of Plaskett. As of 5:59 p.m. Thursday, the fire has burned 140 acres with 0% containment.
Evacuation orders were issued for zones MRY-F035 and MRY-F036. Meanwhile, evacuation warnings have been issued for zones MRY-F033, MRY-F034, and MRY-F037. View evacuation zone map.
"Firefighters from various agencies including U.S. Forest Service, CAL FIRE, and local government are aggressively moving ground crews and heavy equipment to the perimeter of the Plaskett Fire in Monterey County to establish containment lines," officials said in a statement. "Specialized elite Hotshot crews are actively working to gain access to the fire's edge, while eight air tankers have been requested to fly overhead and assist ground personnel with targeted retardant drops."
Officials said Cal Fire's Tulare Charlie Strike Team has been deployed to Los Perros Road to assist about 30 residents, lead evacuation efforts and prepare homes for structure defense. Firefighters are also carrying out evacuations along Burro Road, where five to eight structures may be threatened.
The fire forced the closure of Highway 1 between Old Coast Road at mile marker 50.1 to the north and just north of Gorda at mile marker 10.2 to the south.
The cause of the fire has not been determined.
The Plaskett Fire was burning about 20 miles south of the Timber Fire, which started in the Los Padres National Forest on the night of Aug. 8.
As of Thursday afternoon, the Timber Fire had burned 19,296 acres and was 21% contained, according to Cal Fire. More than 660 structures are threatened, officials said, and the fire has prompted multiple evacuation orders and evacuation warnings.
Officials said the cause of the Timber Fire is under investigation.

sources.news_title: Smoke captured east of Plaskett as new Big Sur vegetation fire breaks out
sources.text:
Plaskett Fire explodes to 1,700 acres, continues moving toward Highway 1
The Plaskett Fire near Gorda has grown to approximately 1,700 acres and remains at zero containment, according to the latest update from CAL FIRE.
The fire continues to move toward Highway 1, with activity concentrated around Willow Creek, just north of Los Burros Road. Firefighters also reported significant growth to the north after the fire crossed Plaskett Ridge and established itself in the canyon behind Pacific Valley.
Ground crews are working to protect threatened properties and create defensible space around structures. Heavy equipment has been deployed to begin building a dozer line from South Coast Ridge Road at Pruitt Ridge down toward the rear of the Pacific Valley Station.
Additional equipment is being brought to construct containment lines along South Coast Ridge Road toward the Los Burros sign, which officials say will help secure the fire’s eastern perimeter.
Overnight crews will focus on structure defense, patrols and perimeter protection. Firefighters will maintain a visible presence along Los Burros Road and Highway 1 while monitoring for spot fires.
Officials say multiple air tankers are assisting with firefighting operations as conditions allow. Six helicopters have also been assigned to the fire.
The cause remains under investigation.
Highway 1 remains closed for approximately 40 miles, from one mile south of Old Coast Road at Milepost 50.1 to north of Gorda at Milepost 10.2. There is no estimated time for the highway to reopen.
The Plaskett Fire prompted an additional closure covering nearly 6 miles, from Milepost 16.0 north of Pacific Valley Ranger Station to Milepost 10.2 near Gorda.
Evacuations
Evacuation orders are in effect for:
- MRY-F035
- MRY-F036
Evacuation warnings are in effect for:
- MRY-F033
- MRY-F034
- MRY-F037
Evacuation orders mean there is an immediate threat to life and residents must leave. Warnings indicate a potential threat to life or property, and people who need additional time to evacuate should leave now.
For evacuees, a shelter is open at the Carmel Mission Inn Conference Room, 3665 Rio Road in Carmel.
For evacuation assistance, call the virtual Temporary Evacuation Point at 831-647-7760.
Stay with KSBW 8 for the latest information.

sources.news_title: Second fire breaks out along Big Sur coast
sources.text:
UPDATE (11:15 a.m.) - According to CAL FIRE. The Plaskett Fire had burned 140 acres and was 0 percent contained as of Thursday morning.
Six helicopters are assigned to the fire.
There have been no reports of injuries or damage to structures.
Evacuation warnings and orders issued Wednesday remain in effect. 
—
ORIGINAL STORY: The Plaskett Fire broke out Wednesday morning along the Big Sur coast, south of the Timber Fire, which has been burning for more than two weeks.
The new fire was first reported at about 11 a.m. east of the community of Plaskett in Monterey County. It is burning in the Los Padres National Forest off Forest Rd 23S10, east of Los Burros Road.
As of 2 p.m., the fire had burned 100 acres, according to CAL FIRE, and was 0% contained.
Fire officials say initial mapping indicates multiple structures may be threatened.
An evacuation order is in effect for zone MRY-F036 in Monterey County.
Evacuation warnings are in place for zones MRY-F035 and MRY-F037.
Firefighters are working to evacuate residents and prepare homes for structure defense.
The cause of the fire is under investigation.
Meanwhile, the Timber Fire has burned more than 17,800 acres since August 8. It was 23% contained as of midday on Wednesday.
Multiple evacuation orders and warnings are in effect. Click here for a map of the zones currently under evacuation.
